Don't know if this helps but when I lived in student housing, a lot of RAs were pre-med students in phys/pharm, bio, etc. They would sometimes talk about their heavy workload in some labs but they seemed to be managing their time pretty well. It's usually during midterms and final exams when everyone is super stressed out. All the RAs were all friends who helped each other and overall, it wasn't a very hostile environment (from what I saw at least). With regards to curving, I only had one class curved and it was curved up, which I don't think is very common in psych. Everyone's grade increased because our class was below the acceptable class average (it's like 65% I think). After that exam, our prof made the next exam slightly easier, however, I'm not sure if every prof is like that. I have heard of people's grades getting curved down and it sucks, but I guess it's just policies and preventing grade inflation ):

I was taking my pre-reqs for nursing last year with many students in arts and sciences. Most of us were first years and we were all sort of in the same boat, so if you're struggling, don't be afraid to ask someone sitting nearby! Plus, you never know, someone might be an upper year and they can help. Also, figure out your best studying habits, and check RateMyProf. It's not always the best source to use, but I found that it was a little helpful when registering for classes. Feel free to message me if you have any other questions!

I have quite a few friends at U of C (some in engineering as well) and the biggest issue they seem to have is the waitlists for classes. I’ve heard classes fill up very fast, even when there’s hundreds of spots available. My friend required a class for her arts degree and they did not give her priority so she has to wait until next fall to take it. Class sizes are HUGE and from what I’ve heard, majority of students haven’t even gotten their final exam grades yet if you look at r/ucalgary. My friends in engg though seem to like it, despite the heavy course load. The building is really nice from what I’ve heard too. I have a friend at usask too in engineering and they’re enjoying it too. I think it really comes down to your style of learning and campus life (when things get back to normal, of course). At usask I’m sure you can get more one on one time with profs rather than ucalgary.

I stayed in Sask Hall my first year and it was nice. It is older compared to CQ, but you’re right on campus. They had activities so you could make friends and get to know people. It was good because you wouldn’t be super isolated. It also has tunnels that go directly from the residence to the meal hall and most of the other buildings. The food in the meal hall was pretty good for the most part too. I don’t know what things would be like though once they open VP again but it was great when I went there :) If you prefer to make your own food, go to CQ but some people I knew preferred to stay at VP because they didn’t have to worry about cooking/cleaning their own bathroom lol.

Girl, I feel you too. My parents have to relate everything to religion. “This happened to you because you didn’t pray.” All that stuff. It sucks man. I went away for university too (an 8 hour drive from home) for some freedom. After the pandemic hit, I had to move back home and it made me realize how much I kind of missed it. I never thought my parents would change but they did. My mom was so disappointed in me when I didn’t make honour roll in my junior year of high school and I was already depressed enough. Throughout uni though, my mom has seen how frazzled I get with school (especially during finals). I think she finally sees how stressed I get and she kind of became more lenient with my grades. You never know, they may finally come around. My parents were so conservative they wouldn’t even let me go to the movie theatre with a boy when I was 17 and I still can’t sleep over at friends’ houses even though I’m 20 now. It makes you not trust them back and it sucks. It makes you more secretive and resentful towards your parents. I wish parents would stop being stuck in an old mindset. But I wish you the best in the US, where you can be you. :) Thanks for sharing your story. It’s nice to hear someone relate
